NASB.1: 'I loathe my own life; I will give full vent to my complaint; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
NASB.2: 'I will say to God, 'Do not condemn me; Let me know why You contend with me.
NASB.3: 'Is it right for You indeed to oppress, To reject the labor of Your hands, And to look favorably on the schemes of the wicked?
NASB.4: 'Have You eyes of flesh? Or do You see as a man sees?
NASB.5: 'Are Your days as the days of a mortal, Or Your years as man's years,
NASB.6: That You should seek for my guilt And search after my sin?
NASB.7: 'According to Your knowledge I am indeed not guilty, Yet there is no deliverance from Your hand.
NASB.8: 'Your hands fashioned and made me altogether, And would You destroy me?
NASB.9: 'Remember now, that You have made me as clay; And would You turn me into dust again?
NASB.10: 'Did You not pour me out like milk And curdle me like cheese;
NASB.11: Clothe me with skin and flesh, And knit me together with bones and sinews?
NASB.12: 'You have granted me life and lovingkindness; And Your care has preserved my spirit.
NASB.13: 'Yet these things You have concealed in Your heart; I know that this is within You:
NASB.14: If I sin, then You would take note of me, And would not acquit me of my guilt.
NASB.15: 'If I am wicked, woe to me! And if I am righteous, I dare not lift up my head. [I am] sated with disgrace and conscious of my misery.
NASB.16: 'Should [my head] be lifted up, You would hunt me like a lion; And again You would show Your power against me.
NASB.17: 'You renew Your witnesses against me And increase Your anger toward me; Hardship after hardship is with me.
NASB.18: 'Why then have You brought me out of the womb? Would that I had died and no eye had seen me!
NASB.19: 'I should have been as though I had not been, Carried from womb to tomb.'
NASB.20: 'Would He not let my few days alone? Withdraw from me that I may have a little cheer
NASB.21: Before I go-- and I shall not return-- To the land of darkness and deep shadow,
NASB.22: The land of utter gloom as darkness [itself], Of deep shadow without order, And which shines as the darkness.'

ESV.1: “I loathe my life; I will give free utterance to my complaint; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
ESV.2: I will say to God, Do not condemn me; let me know why you contend against me.
ESV.3: Does it seem good to you to oppress, to despise the work of your hands and favor the designs of the wicked?
ESV.4: Have you eyes of flesh? Do you see as man sees?
ESV.5: Are your days as the days of man, or your years as a man's years,
ESV.6: that you seek out my iniquity and search for my sin,
ESV.7: although you know that I am not guilty, and there is none to deliver out of your hand?
ESV.8: Your hands fashioned and made me, and now you have destroyed me altogether.
ESV.9: Remember that you have made me like clay; and will you return me to the dust?
ESV.10: Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese?
ESV.11: You clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews.
ESV.12: You have granted me life and steadfast love, and your care has preserved my spirit.
ESV.13: Yet these things you hid in your heart; I know that this was your purpose.
ESV.14: If I sin, you watch me and do not acquit me of my iniquity.
ESV.15: If I am guilty, woe to me! If I am in the right, I cannot lift up my head, for I am filled with disgrace and look on my affliction.
ESV.16: And were my head lifted up,  you would hunt me like a lion and again work wonders against me.
ESV.17: You renew your witnesses against me and increase your vexation toward me; you bring fresh troops against me.
ESV.18: “Why did you bring me out from the womb? Would that I had died before any eye had seen me
ESV.19: and were as though I had not been, carried from the womb to the grave.
ESV.20: Are not my days few? Then cease, and leave me alone, that I may find a little cheer
ESV.21: before I go — and I shall not return — to the land of darkness and deep shadow,
ESV.22: the land of gloom like thick darkness, like deep shadow without any order, where light is as thick darkness.”

AMP.1:
"I am disgusted with my life and loathe it!
I will give free expression to my complaint;
I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
AMP.2:
"I will say to God, 'Do not condemn me [and declare me guilty]!
Show me why You contend and argue and struggle with me.
AMP.3:
'Does it indeed seem right to You to oppress,
To despise and reject the work of Your hands,
And to look with favor on the schemes of the wicked?
AMP.4:
'Do You have eyes of flesh?
Do You see as a man sees?
AMP.5:
'Are Your days as the days of a mortal,
Are Your years as man's years,
AMP.6:
That You seek my guilt
And search for my sin?
AMP.7:
'Although You know that I am not guilty or wicked,
Yet there is no one who can rescue me from Your hand.
AMP.8:
'Your hands have formed and made me altogether.
Would You [turn around and] destroy me?
AMP.9:
'Remember now, that You have made me as clay;
So will You turn me into dust again?
AMP.10:
'Have You not poured me out like milk
And curdled me like cheese?
AMP.11:
'[You have] clothed me with skin and flesh,
And knit me together with bones and sinews.
AMP.12:
'You have granted me life and lovingkindness;
And Your providence (divine care, supervision) has preserved my spirit.
AMP.13:
'Yet these [present evils] You have hidden in Your heart [since my creation]:
I know that this was within You [in Your purpose and thought].
AMP.14:
'If I sin, then You would take note and observe me,
And You would not acquit me of my guilt.
AMP.15:
'If I am wicked, woe to me [for judgment comes]!
And if I am righteous, I dare not lift up my head.
For I am sated and filled with disgrace and the sight of my misery.
AMP.16:
'Should I lift my head up, You would hunt me like a lion;
And again You would show Your marvelous power against me.
AMP.17:
'You renew Your witnesses against me
And increase Your indignation and anger toward me;
Hardship after hardship is with me [attacking me time after time].
AMP.18:
'Why then did You bring me out of the womb?
Would that I had perished and no eye had seen me!
AMP.19:
'I should have been as though I had not existed;
[I should have been] carried from the womb to the grave.'
AMP.20:
"Would He not let my few days alone,
Withdraw from me that I may have a little cheer
AMP.21:
Before I go—and I shall not return—
To the land of darkness and the deep shadow [of death],
AMP.22:
The [sunless] land of utter gloom as darkness itself,
[The land] of the shadow of death, without order,
And [where] it shines as [thick] darkness."

NLT.1:
“I am disgusted with my life.
Let me complain freely.
My bitter soul must complain.
NLT.2:
I will say to God, ‘Don’t simply condemn me —
tell me the charge you are bringing against me.
NLT.3:
What do you gain by oppressing me?
Why do you reject me, the work of your own hands,
while smiling on the schemes of the wicked?
NLT.4:
Are your eyes like those of a human?
Do you see things only as people see them?
NLT.5:
Is your lifetime only as long as ours?
Is your life so short
NLT.6:
that you must quickly probe for my guilt
and search for my sin?
NLT.7:
Although you know I am not guilty,
no one can rescue me from your hands.
NLT.8:
“‘You formed me with your hands; you made me,
yet now you completely destroy me.
NLT.9:
Remember that you made me from dust —
will you turn me back to dust so soon?
NLT.10:
You guided my conception
and formed me in the womb.
NLT.11:
You clothed me with skin and flesh,
and you knit my bones and sinews together.
NLT.12:
You gave me life and showed me your unfailing love.
My life was preserved by your care.
NLT.14:
was to watch me, and if I sinned,
you would not forgive my guilt.
NLT.15:
If I am guilty, too bad for me;
and even if I’m innocent, I can’t hold my head high,
because I am filled with shame and misery.
NLT.16:
And if I hold my head high, you hunt me like a lion
and display your awesome power against me.
NLT.17:
Again and again you witness against me.
You pour out your growing anger on me
and bring fresh armies against me.
NLT.18:
“‘Why, then, did you deliver me from my mother’s womb?
Why didn’t you let me die at birth?
NLT.19:
It would be as though I had never existed,
going directly from the womb to the grave.
NLT.20:
I have only a few days left, so leave me alone,
that I may have a moment of comfort
NLT.21:
before I leave — never to return —
for the land of darkness and utter gloom.
NLT.22:
It is a land as dark as midnight,
a land of gloom and confusion,
where even the light is dark as midnight.’”

MSG.1:
"I can't stand my life—I hate it!
-I'm putting it all out on the table,
all the bitterness of my life—I'm holding back nothing."
MSG.2:
Job prayed:
"Here's what I want to say:
Don't, God, bring in a verdict of guilty
without letting me know the charges you're bringing.
MSG.3:
How does this fit into what you once called 'good'—
giving me a hard time, spurning me,
a life you shaped by your very own hands,
and then blessing the plots of the wicked?
MSG.4:
You don't look at things the way we mortals do.
You're not taken in by appearances, are you?
MSG.5:
Unlike us, you're not working against a deadline.
You have all eternity to work things out.
MSG.6:
So what's this all about, anyway—this compulsion
to dig up some dirt, to find some skeleton in my closet?
MSG.7:
You know good and well I'm not guilty.
You also know no one can help me.
MSG.8:
"You made me like a handcrafted piece of pottery—
and now are you going to smash me to pieces?
MSG.9:
Don't you remember how beautifully you worked my clay?
Will you reduce me now to a mud pie?
MSG.10:
Oh, that marvel of conception as you stirred together
semen and ovum—
MSG.11:
What a miracle of skin and bone,
muscle and brain!
MSG.12:
You gave me life itself, and incredible love.
You watched and guarded every breath I took.
MSG.13:
"But you never told me about this part.
I should have known that there was more to it—
MSG.14:
That if I so much as missed a step, you'd notice and pounce,
wouldn't let me get by with a thing.
MSG.15:
If I'm truly guilty, I'm doomed.
But if I'm innocent, it's no better—I'm still doomed.
My belly is full of bitterness.
I'm up to my ears in a swamp of affliction.
MSG.16:
I try to make the best of it, try to brave it out,
but you're too much for me,
relentless, like a lion on the prowl.
MSG.17:
You line up fresh witnesses against me.
You compound your anger
and pile on the grief and pain!
MSG.18:
"So why did you have me born?
I wish no one had ever laid eyes on me!
MSG.19:
I wish I'd never lived—a stillborn,
buried without ever having breathed.
MSG.20:
Isn't it time to call it quits on my life?
Can't you let up, and let me smile just once
MSG.21:
Before I die and am buried,
before I'm nailed into my coffin, sealed in the ground,
MSG.22:
And banished for good to the land of the dead,
blind in the final dark?"

NET.5: Are your days like the days of a mortal, or your years like the years of a mortal,
NET.6: that you must search out my iniquity, and inquire about my sin,
NET.7: although you know that I am not guilty, and that there is no one who can deliver out of your hand?
NET.8: “Your hands have shaped me and made me, but now you destroy me completely.
NET.9: Remember that you have made me as with the clay; will you return me to dust?
NET.10: Did you not pour me out like milk, and curdle me like cheese?
NET.11: You clothed me with skin and flesh and knit me together with bones and sinews.
NET.12: You gave me life and favor, and your intervention watched over my spirit.
NET.13: “But these things you have concealed in your heart; I know that this is with you:
NET.14: If I sinned, then you would watch me and you would not acquit me of my iniquity.
NET.15: If I am guilty, woe to me, and if I am innocent, I cannot lift my head; I am full of shame, and satiated with my affliction.
NET.16: If I lift myself up, you hunt me as a fierce lion, and again you display your power against me.
NET.17: You bring new witnesses against me, and increase your anger against me; relief troops come against me.
NET.18: “Why then did you bring me out from the womb? I should have died and no eye would have seen me!
NET.19: I should have been as though I had never existed; I should have been carried right from the womb to the grave!
NET.20: Are not my days few? Cease, then, and leave me alone, that I may find a little comfort,
NET.21: before I depart, never to return, to the land of darkness and the deepest shadow,
NET.22: to the land of utter darkness, like the deepest darkness, and the deepest shadow and disorder, where even the light is like darkness.”

NRSVCE.1:
“I loathe my life;
I will give free utterance to my complaint;
I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
NRSVCE.2:
I will say to God, Do not condemn me;
let me know why you contend against me.
NRSVCE.3:
Does it seem good to you to oppress,
to despise the work of your hands
and favor the schemes of the wicked?
NRSVCE.4:
Do you have eyes of flesh?
Do you see as humans see?
NRSVCE.5:
Are your days like the days of mortals,
or your years like human years,
NRSVCE.6:
that you seek out my iniquity
and search for my sin,
NRSVCE.7:
although you know that I am not guilty,
and there is no one to deliver out of your hand?
NRSVCE.8:
Your hands fashioned and made me;
and now you turn and destroy me.
NRSVCE.9:
Remember that you fashioned me like clay;
and will you turn me to dust again?
NRSVCE.10:
Did you not pour me out like milk
and curdle me like cheese?
NRSVCE.11:
You clothed me with skin and flesh,
and knit me together with bones and sinews.
NRSVCE.12:
You have granted me life and steadfast love,
and your care has preserved my spirit.
NRSVCE.13:
Yet these things you hid in your heart;
I know that this was your purpose.
NRSVCE.14:
If I sin, you watch me,
and do not acquit me of my iniquity.
NRSVCE.15:
If I am wicked, woe to me!
If I am righteous, I cannot lift up my head,
for I am filled with disgrace
and look upon my affliction.
NRSVCE.16:
Bold as a lion you hunt me;
you repeat your exploits against me.
NRSVCE.17:
You renew your witnesses against me,
and increase your vexation toward me;
you bring fresh troops against me.
NRSVCE.18:
“Why did you bring me forth from the womb?
Would that I had died before any eye had seen me,
NRSVCE.19:
and were as though I had not been,
carried from the womb to the grave.
NRSVCE.20:
Are not the days of my life few?
Let me alone, that I may find a little comfort
NRSVCE.21:
before I go, never to return,
to the land of gloom and deep darkness,
NRSVCE.22:
the land of gloom and chaos,
where light is like darkness.”
